newsitem.title: USA: Global PC unit shipments rise 16 pct in Q1 - IDC.
newsitem.headline: Global PC unit shipments rise 16 pct in Q1 - IDC.

text.p: Global unit shipments of personal computers jumped 16 percent over the first quarter of 1996, according to research firm International Data Corp.
By comparison, IDC said that Worldwide shipments rose by 13 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 against the year before.
IDC said U.S. shipments marked a 20 percent rise, the fastest of any major region, and the best quarterly domestic growth rate since the end of 1995.
The firm attributed the sales growth to new products, including those with powerful multimedia chips and systems costing less than $1000, as well as high-end portables PCs.
Compaq Computer Corp continued to be the global sales leader, with an 11.1 percent share, the report said.
International Business Machines Corp was second in global sales, while Dell Computer Corp was third.
All three of the firms scored an increase in units shipped and market share in 1997's first quarter, compared to the same period in 1996, IDC said.
The research firm said PC shipments in Western Europe rose 13 percent in the quarter, on stronger corporate buying.

Economic uncertainty weighed upon sales in major Asian markets, holding shipment growth in Japan to 14 percent and in the rest of the Asia/Pacific region to 13 percent, unusually low for that fast-growing part of the world, IDC said.
Demand was stronger in Japan than the shipment numbers indicate, however, as businesses were unable to buy all the systems they wanted due to a shortage of notebook PCs.
